timed_region: Each rank times the complete qtClustering call, including device setup, distributed clustering, result construction, and cleanup (qtclustering/qtclustering.cpp:441-447). Validation and external result printing occur afterward; benchmark mode uses the same computation.
start_synchronization: The root-issued fused-mode broadcast inside qtClustering gates subsequent useful computation on every rank (qtclustering/qtclustering.cpp:187-202). Root starts timing before issuing it, so the absence of a start barrier does not defeat the start-boundary proof.
stop_synchronization: Blocking device-to-host copies complete candidate kernels before their results enter MPI collectives (qtclustering/qtclustering.cpp:252-262, 273-279). However, after the terminal collective, ranks still construct final clusters: either the singleton-emission loop or the final cluster assembly and membership updates (265-286). A nonroot can perform this work after root returns and stops timing. No completion dependency encloses that tail across ranks.
rank_aggregation: Every rank obtains a complete local duration, but none is reduced. MPI_MAXLOC at line 262 combines candidate counts and seed indices, not elapsed times. The exit-code broadcast at line 505 occurs after root has stopped and printed its timer.
reported_value: The canonical Clustering time line prints only rank 0's cluster_time.count(), in milliseconds (qtclustering/qtclustering.cpp:445-451).
semantic_equivalence_basis: This is cooperative computation, not independent complete-result replication. At the benchmark configuration of 5000 points and four ranks, each rank evaluates only its 1250 owned seeds. Global candidate selection and selected-member broadcasts supply results computed by other ranks. Although the initial broadcast establishes a valid root start boundary, the final collective does not enclose all subsequent clustering work, so root's interval is not a proven global makespan.

evidence.finding: Seed ownership is rank-strided; candidate evaluations cover only locally owned seeds and require a global MAXLOC selection.
The root-issued fused-mode broadcast precedes useful computation on every rank and occurs inside root's timed call.
A blocking device-to-host copy completes each candidate batch before local selection and the global candidate reduction.

Both termination paths contain algorithmic host work after their last collective: singleton cluster generation, or selected-cluster construction and membership updates. Root has no dependency on completion of this tail on other ranks.
The winning owner's kernel completes through a blocking copy before broadcasting members. Each rank finishes its own result construction and device cleanup before returning.
Local timers surround qtClustering on every rank, but only root's unaggregated duration is printed.
Result printing and validation are outside timing; neither changes clustering dispatch. The subsequent exit-code broadcast cannot extend the already-stopped timer.

minimal_fix: After every rank computes cluster_time and before entering the rank-0 output block, reduce local_ms = cluster_time.count() with MPI_Reduce using MPI_LONG and MPI_MAX. Print the reduced maximum under Clustering time.
notes: The supplied target-platform evidence establishes that the millisecond count has C++ type long, so the existing %ld formatting and the proposed MPI_LONG reduction match this target. Whole-millisecond formatting is not a timing defect. No tools or execution were used.
